modality_or_therapeutic_area: Small molecule androgen receptor antagonist (enzalutamide / XTANDI)

Medivation 8-K response, April 2016 — rejection of Sanofi proposal

Medivation's Board of Directors unanimously rejected as not in the best interests of the company and its stockholders, a new unsolicited proposal to acquire Medivation.
why_catchable_or_not: Public unsolicited proposal was disclosed in 8-K and press release on April 28, 2016 — 116 days before Pfizer announcement. EDGAR-catchable with standard process-signal keyword scan.

Board rejection publicly disclosed
Company-level process — not asset-specific

Competitive bidding environment following public rejection

buyer_strategic_rationale: Pfizer sought oncology franchise expansion via enzalutamide and pipeline diversification with talazoparib
target_strategic_rationale: Medivation board resisted Sanofi's initial price; competitive auction achieved superior value for shareholders
catalyst_context: Enzalutamide already approved and generating >$2B annual revenue; talazoparib Phase 3 catalyst upcoming
valuation_context: Pfizer paid $81.50/share vs Sanofi's initial $52.50/share — 55% increase driven by competitive process
price_reaction_context: Stock rallied sharply on Sanofi proposal announcement; further appreciation on Pfizer announcement
competing_bid_context: Sanofi initially proposed; multiple parties entered; Pfizer ultimately won at $81.50/share
activist_context: Activists supported sale process following Sanofi's public proposal
banker_or_advisor_context: Medivation retained financial advisors following Sanofi's public approach

true_signal_lessons: Public unsolicited proposal in 8-K is the clearest pre-announcement signal type — EDGAR-catchable

Named acquirer + company-level language = highest confidence signal
116-day lead time shows public process signal can persist well before definitive deal
operator_lesson: Any public unsolicited acquisition proposal in 8-K or press release for a commercial-stage biotech is a P5_HIGH_PRIORITY_PROCESS_SIGNAL. Read the filing immediately and track subsequent board responses.
model_training_summary: MDVN is the canonical TRUE_PUBLIC_PRIOR_SIGNAL example. Sanofi's public $52.50 proposal on April 28, 2016 was disclosed 116 days before Pfizer's $81.50 definitive agreement. EDGAR-catchable. Board rejection followed by competitive auction. Key signal: named acquirer, explicit price in press release, company-level scope.

Ultragenyx press release and Dimension 8-K, October 3 2017 — definitive agreement

why_catchable_or_not: Superior proposal determination disclosed in 8-K on October 2, 2017 — one day before definitive Ultragenyx announcement. EDGAR-catchable. However lead time was only ~1 day from public superior proposal to definitive deal. Earlier REGENXBIO merger agreement was the prior public setup context.
visible_setup_traits: Explicit 'Superior Proposal' language in 8-K — clearest possible signal type
Named competing acquirer (Ultragenyx) and named incumbent party (REGENXBIO) both disclosed
Explicit share price ($6.00) in public filing
Company-level transaction — full acquisition
Prior merger agreement (REGENXBIO) created public context for competing bid
REGENXBIO waiver of matching rights also disclosed publicly same day
invisible_setup_traits: Ultragenyx's approach to Dimension prior to public superior proposal was private
Negotiation terms between parties were not disclosed until proxy
buyer_strategic_rationale: Ultragenyx sought to expand gene therapy platform; Dimension's AAV manufacturing capabilities and hemophilia pipeline were strategically complementary
target_strategic_rationale: Dimension was already in a merger process with REGENXBIO; Ultragenyx's superior proposal created obligation to declare fiduciary out
catalyst_context: Gene therapy M&A wave 2016-2018; AAV manufacturing scarcity made Dimension platform valuable
valuation_context: $6.00/share from Ultragenyx vs REGENXBIO's prior deal price; board determined superior on value and certainty
price_reaction_context: Stock moved on superior proposal disclosure one day before definitive agreement
competing_bid_context: Classic go-shop / superior proposal scenario: REGENXBIO merger agreement had no-shop with fiduciary out; Ultragenyx exercised the fiduciary out; REGENXBIO declined to match
banker_or_advisor_context: Both parties retained advisors for the competitive process
partnership_or_rights_context: REGENXBIO had existing collaboration rights with Dimension prior to merger agreement
asset_specific_vs_company_level: Company-level — entire Dimension acquired including AAV platform
false_positive_lessons: Superior proposal language in proxy BACKGROUND section (post-announcement) is not a pre-announcement signal — distinguish from 8-K superior proposal filing
true_signal_lessons: Superior proposal determination in 8-K = immediate P5_HIGH_PRIORITY_PROCESS_SIGNAL
Named acquirer + explicit price = minimal ambiguity
Even 1-day lead time from superior proposal filing to definitive deal is a valid edge window
Prior merger agreement creates visible context for competing bid monitoring
operator_lesson: Monitor 8-Ks for 'Superior Proposal' and 'Competing Proposal' language for companies that already have pending merger agreements. These are near-definitive signals with very short windows.
model_training_summary: DMTX is the canonical COMPETING_BID_OR_SUPERIOR_PROPOSAL example. Ultragenyx's superior proposal was publicly disclosed in an 8-K on October 2, 2017 — one day before definitive deal. Superior proposal language is EDGAR-catchable and nearly unambiguous. Prior REGENXBIO merger context was also public.
